verses.verse:
बद्धाय जीवाय निबद्धगानम् मुक्ताय जीवाय विमुक्त गानम्।
अद्वैत भावेन विमुक्त गानम् द्वैत प्रघानं तु निबद्ध गानम्।१३०।
verses.text: For the bound soul, bound singing; for the free soul, free singing. Free singing comes from a sense of non-duality; bound singing is ruled by duality.

commentary.text: Although there is no being in this world who is completely free, still some are more bound and some less. So the free being prefers free singing (mukta gāna) and open places, and bound beings prefer nibaddha gāna (bound, metred singing) and well-enclosed places.

Just as a thing is tied up securely when it is moved from one place to another, so the singer's rāga, which in the form of ālāpa was 'svāntaḥ sukhāya' (for one's own inner joy), is now going to be bound in tāla for 'parānta sukhāya' (for the joy of others). So bound music cannot be carried on without two persons. These two kinds are usually as much in dispute as the doctrines of non-duality (advaitavāda) and duality (dvaitavāda). To be free of these disputes, adopting the baṛā khayāl as a reconciling view (sāmyavāda) would suit the age. That is why khayāl singing is more widespread than dhrupad singing, for too much bondage (bandhan) is held to be a cause of wailing (krandan).
